jobs.title: Vice President, Enterprise Platforms
jobs.description:
The Klick Group
—comprising Klick Health (including Klick Katalyst and btwelve), Klick Media Group, Klick Applied Sciences (including Klick Labs), Klick Consulting, and Klick Ventures—is an ecosystem dedicated to realizing the full potential of our people and clients in life sciences. Founded in 1997, we have offices in New York, Philadelphia, Saratoga Springs, Toronto, London, São Paulo, and Singapore. Consistently named a Best Managed Company, Most Admired Corporate Culture, and Great Place to Work, Klick is committed to fostering a high-performance, people-first culture with creativity, collaboration, innovation, and impact across everything we do.

About Our Technology Craft

Our Technology Craft powers Klick’s innovation through platforms, products, and emerging technologies. This craft enables scale, efficiency, and experimentation across the business. Technology teams transform ideas into functional, future-ready solutions. Their work supports both client delivery and internal growth.

Job Description

The Vice President, Enterprise Platforms leads enterprise architecture, client solutioning, and pre-sales strategy for pharmaceutical and life sciences organizations. This role bridges sales opportunity ownership with hands-on technical leadership, shaping complex omnichannel ecosystems that drive measurable business impact. The position partners closely with Sales, Strategy, Medical, Media, and Delivery teams to position technology as a differentiator in multi-million-dollar pursuits while establishing scalable architecture standards.

What You’ll Do

Lead enterprise pre-sales strategy, pipeline forecasting, and opportunity management for multi-million-dollar pharmaceutical platform engagements in collaboration with Sales and Account teams.
Facilitate executive discovery workshops and roadmap sessions with senior pharma stakeholders to define CRM, marketing automation, and data architecture strategies.
Design end-to-end omnichannel architectures spanning Salesforce, Veeva, Adobe, Marketo, SFMC, Snowflake, Databricks, Fabric, CDPs, APIs, and integration layers.
Produce architecture diagrams, interaction models, data flows, solution specifications, pricing estimates, and SOW documentation aligned to client and delivery requirements.
Establish governance frameworks, architecture standards, and AI-enabled solution patterns while guiding steering committees and mentoring internal architecture teams.

Qualifications

Required:

10+ years of experience in pharmaceutical or life sciences technology, consulting, or enterprise sales operations with demonstrated ownership of complex client engagements.
5+ years of hands-on enterprise architecture or solution design experience, including documented architecture diagrams, data models, and technical specifications.
Proven experience leading pre-sales efforts and managing pipeline for multi-million-dollar opportunities, including forecasting and proposal development.
Deep expertise in enterprise platforms such as Salesforce, Veeva, Adobe Experience Cloud, Marketo, SFMC, Snowflake, Databricks, Microsoft Fabric, or comparable ecosystems.
Demonstrated experience presenting technical strategies and architecture roadmaps to senior client stakeholders and executive steering committees.

Desired:

Comfort and enthusiasm for using AI as a regular part of how work gets done.
Experience applying AI/ML solutions such as next-best-action, personalization models, predictive analytics, or generative AI for content modularization and insight automation.
Formal training or certification in architecture frameworks such as TOGAF, SAFe, or equivalent enterprise methodologies.
Experience establishing architecture governance processes and reference models within regulated industries.

This posting is for an existing vacancy at Klick.

jobs.description:

As Director, Data Scouting, you will lead the strategy, governance, and commercial management of CPP Investments' external data portfolio. Reporting to the Managing Director, you will partner with investment teams and enterprise stakeholders to optimize external data sourcing, vendor relationships, and commercial outcomes. You will lead a team of market data professionals while driving transparency, operational excellence, and value across the firm's external data investments.

The Team

Technology & Operations enables CPP Investments to deliver on its global investment mandate by providing secure, innovative, and data-driven technology capabilities. The department partners across the organization to deliver trusted data, modern platforms, and strategic technology services that enhance investment decision-making and operational excellence.

The Data Scouting team is responsible for the strategy, sourcing, governance, and commercial management of external data across CPP Investments. Working closely with investment teams and enterprise partners, the team ensures external data is accessible, cost-effective, and aligned with business priorities while maximizing the value of the firm's data investments.

Accountabilities

Develop and execute the strategy for CPP Investments' external data portfolio, ensuring data products align with evolving business needs while improving value, transparency, and portfolio efficiency.
Provide strategic advice to investment teams and enterprise stakeholders on external data sourcing, vendor capabilities, and commercial models to support informed investment decisions.
Lead the evaluation, negotiation, and management of complex third-party data contracts, ensuring commercial value, consistency, compliance, and effective risk management.
Build and manage strategic relationships with external data providers, driving vendor performance, governance, innovation, and long-term partnership value.
Identify opportunities to optimize external data spend through portfolio rationalization, contract consolidation, product substitution, and disciplined cost management.
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team while fostering a collaborative, inclusive culture focused on continuous improvement and professional growth.
Influence senior stakeholders and lead cross-functional initiatives that strengthen governance, standardize processes, and advance CPP Investments' external data strategy.

What You Bring

Undergraduate degree or equivalent combination of education and experience in Business, Finance, Information Management, Technology, or a related discipline.
Significant experience leading market data, vendor management, strategic sourcing, procurement, or commercial management functions within a complex organization.
Demonstrated success negotiating high-value, complex commercial agreements and managing strategic supplier relationships.
Strong commercial judgment with experience optimizing costs, managing vendor performance, and delivering measurable business value.
Deep understanding of the market data vendor landscape, commercial licensing models, and industry best practices.
Proven leadership experience developing high-performing teams and influencing senior stakeholders across matrixed organizations.
CFA, CAIA, or equivalent investment domain knowledge is considered an asset.

You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.

jobs.description:

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

Reporting to the Vice-President, HR Business Partner, Digital, Client Experience and Operations Transformation, the AVP, Program Management & Transformation is a senior leadership role responsible for translating the people and workplace transformation agenda into coordinated, measurable execution across a complex portfolio of business, technology and operations teams.

The role is the central orchestration point for priority people and workplace transformations. It establishes the plans, governance, management routines and cross-functional accountability required to move work from strategy to sustained delivery, while connecting workforce planning, organizational effectiveness, employee experience, data, talent and change.

This is a high-impact role for a pragmatic executive leader who combines transformation expertise, disciplined program management, organizational judgment and strong influence without authority.

Please note this role requires regular presence at our Toronto One York office

What will you do:

Transformation Program Leadership & Enterprise Delivery

Lead integrated execution across the portfolio's highest-priority workplace transformation programs, translating strategy into actionable plans with clear outcomes, ownership, milestones and value measures.
Act as the drumbeat behind delivery, maintaining momentum week over week and proactively identifying risks, dependencies, resource constraints and decisions before they become barriers.
Coordinate senior leaders, HRBPs, Centres of Expertise, Finance, Talent Acquisition, Data and Analytics, Technology and business workstream owners to align priorities and resolve blockers without direct authority.
Establish fit-for-purpose governance, decision forums, risk registers, integrated roadmaps and escalation paths that accelerate execution while preserving appropriate people and risk considerations.
Monitor progress against strategic commitments and provide executive-level recommendations on priorities, trade-offs and interventions required.

OKR Governance, Performance & Measurement

Design and lead a connected OKR governance approach spanning Canadian business units, functions and HR, with clear standards, cadences, ownership and escalation mechanisms.
Connect OKRs to the enterprise metrics agenda and performance culture, building the capability and tools leaders need to set high-quality objectives and use data to improve performance.
Define value measures across workstreams, integrating workforce, organizational health, employee experience and business indicators into a trusted view of delivery.
Develop executive dashboards, portfolio reviews and management routines that create transparency, surface root causes and drive timely corrective action.

Workforce Strategy & People Process Alignment

Lead cross-business workforce planning grounded in labour supply and demand, capability gaps and build-versus-buy choices, with short-, medium- and long-term talent requirements.
Partner with HRBPs, Talent Acquisition and Finance to assess hiring pipeline health, fill-rate risks and talent investment effectiveness, and sponsor targeted improvement initiatives.
Align role, level, compensation and talent evaluation approaches to external technology and AI markets while maintaining enterprise consistency.
Integrate workforce transition and capability-building plans into transformation roadmaps, connecting the work to enterprise Talent mechanisms.

Employee Experience, Change & Ways of Working

Embed employee experience and data and analytics into program design, using evidence to understand workforce needs, anticipate friction and improve adoption and outcomes.
Lead the change approach for complex transformations, including stakeholder segmentation, communications, readiness, transition support and sustained adoption.
Assess the cumulative impact of change on leaders, teams and HR, and sequence work to protect delivery capacity, employee trust and business continuity.
Advance new ways of working across the Canadian organization, simplifying how work moves across organizational boundaries and strengthening accountability, pace and collaboration.

Executive Partnership & Organizational Enablement

Serve as a trusted advisor to the VP HRBP and senior business and HR leaders, bringing structured problem solving, sound judgment and a clear enterprise perspective to ambiguous issues.
Define effective connection points with Strategy and Enablement, Employee Experience, Data and Analytics, Talent and other HR capabilities so accountability is clear and work is integrated end to end.
Prepare concise, decision-oriented materials for the VP HRBP, CHRO, senior leadership and governance forums, translating complex work into clear implications and recommendations.
Facilitate cross-functional working sessions that align leaders, accelerate decisions and convert insight into action.
Lead and develop a high-performing team and project community while promoting collaboration, inclusion and continuous improvement.

What Do You Need To Succeed

10+ years of progressive experience in transformation, enterprise program leadership, strategy execution, organizational effectiveness, consulting, HR transformation or a related field.
Demonstrated success leading complex, cross-functional transformation programs in a large, matrixed organization, with measurable results and sustained adoption.
Strong program and portfolio management capability, including integrated planning, governance, dependency and risk management, value realization and executive reporting.
Experience shaping workforce strategy, organizational change and people transformation across business, technology and operations environments.
Proven ability to influence VP- and SVP-level stakeholders, navigate competing priorities and drive accountability without direct authority.
Experience with OKRs, performance measurement, employee experience and data-informed decision-making, combined with an understanding of AI-enabled transformation.
Post-secondary education in a related discipline or equivalent experience.

Leadership Profile

The successful candidate will be:

A pragmatic transformation leader who turns strategy into action, pace and measurable outcomes.
A systems thinker who can connect strategy, workforce, performance, employee experience, data and change.
A disciplined operator who creates clarity, anticipates dependencies and follows through on commitments.
A trusted advisor with the judgment and executive presence to influence senior leaders and resolve difficult trade-offs.
A data-driven decision-maker who uses evidence to diagnose issues, measure progress and recommend interventions.
An exceptional communicator who simplifies complexity and creates clear, decision-oriented narratives.
A collaborative people leader who develops talent and models accountability, inclusion and continuous improvement.

Who We Are Looking For

Join the Financial Reporting team and direct the reporting cycles and filings of various clients. You will ensure that client financial statements are in accordance with the rules and regulations that drive financial statement disclosures and other regulatory filings. You will manage the preparation and review of client quarterly, semi-annual and annual financial statements, regulatory filings and other periodic reporting by our staff and our offshore teams. You will engage with clients, auditors and other State Street teams to resolve issues and answer inquiries to ready client financial statements and filings for finalization.

Why this role is important to us

The team you will be joining is a part of State Street Global Services (SSGS). SSGS gives asset owners and managers access to the essential financial tools they need to deliver effective investment solutions. From core custody, accounting, fund administration and shareholder recordkeeping, to complete operations solutions and servicing for alternative assets like OTC derivatives, private equity and real estate, SSGS’ tools help our clients make better investment choices and act on growth opportunities.

Join us if making your mark in the financial services industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.

What You Will Be Responsible For

As Financial Reporting, Assistant Vice President you will

Manage a diverse group of personnel involved in the preparation of interim / annual financial statements for alternative investments products (e.g. hedge, private equity, real estate, fund of funds, business development companies).
Lead, direct and manage the department in collaboration with your manager and senior colleagues
Act as the primary point of escalation for clients with responsibility for implementing and supporting the service requirements of the various client relationships serviced within the group
Work internally in allocating clients and resources within the team
Collaborate with the clients and colleagues globally as appropriate to service clients and/or projects
Responsible for the effective recruitment, training, development and retention of a team of managers who are responsible for meeting their client’s financial reporting needs and effectively managing their team members
Develop and retain personal and team talent.
Act as a source of technical support and guidance to the team, other State Street internal teams and the client. This includes reviewing of files prepared by the teams.
Work with other members of the team in setting individual and team targets and priorities; maintain high standards of client service; conduct performance appraisals and give feedback on individual and team performance
Effective messaging and communication
Participate in team specific and department wide projects as required from time to time
Perform other duties as required in order to meet client and department deliverables/goals

What We Value

These skills will help you succeed in this role

Experience managing a team.
Ability to develop business relationships, both within and outside of the organization. Excellent interpersonal, organizational and communication skills.
Demonstrates an ability to be a leader on their team, as well as be a leader amongst your peers in the department.
Knowledge of Securities Exchange Commission (SEC), Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) requirements and laws as they apply to investment companies, Trusts, Partnerships and other fund structures.
Ability to effectively handle and resolve numerous ongoing communications and reporting deliverables in fast paced environment.
Ability to drive change and process improvements, while managing day-to-day activities in a reporting cycle.
Ability to communicate effectively with clients regarding their financial statements, regulatory disclosures and process improvements (standardization of disclosures and automation).
Ability to effectively manage a team of professionals, planning out work and resource allocation. Provide feedback and development.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

BS degree in Accounting, Business, or related field. CPA or MBA is preferred.
Six or more years of experience in alternative funds fund administration function (financial reporting preferred) or accounting, audit or related business activity.

About State Street

What we do.
State Street is one of the largest custodian banks, asset managers and asset intelligence companies in the world. From technology to product innovation we’re making our mark on the financial services industry. For more than two centuries, we’ve been helping our clients safeguard and steward the investments of millions of people. We provide investment servicing, data & analytics, investment research & trading and investment management to institutional clients.

We warmly welcome the candidates of diverse origin, background, ability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity and personality. You will have tools to help balance your professional and personal life, paid volunteer days, matching gift program and access to employee networks that help you stay connected to what matters to you.

jobs.description:
Choose a workplace that empowers your impact.

Join a global workplace where employees thrive. One that embraces diversity of thought, expertise and experience. A place where you can personalize your employee journey to be — and deliver — your best.

We are a purpose-driven, dynamic and sustainable pension plan. An industry leading global investor with teams in Toronto to London, New York, Singapore, Sydney and other major cities across North America and Europe. We embody the values of our 665,000 members, placing their best interests at the heart of everything we do.

Join us to accelerate your growth & development, prioritize wellness, build connections, and support the communities where we live and work.

Don’t just work anywhere — come build tomorrow together with us.

Know someone at OMERS or Oxford Properties?
Great! If you're referred, have them submit your name through Workday first. Then, watch for a unique link in your email to apply.

The Associate Director, Internal Audit provides both strategic leadership and hands-on execution across pension operations and technology-focused audit and project assurance activities. Our Pension system modernization and automation has been critical to keeping pace with the service requirements of our growing membership base and is a critical strategic objective to support our OMERS 2030 strategy. This role bridges audit delivery with advisory leadership, overseeing high-impact, risk-based audits while providing consultative guidance on governance, risk management, and control environments across both the operations and technology in Pensions. The role works closely with senior leaders across the business, technology, and second-line oversight functions, and supports the Director and IA leadership in shaping audit strategy, identifying emerging risks, and strengthening the overall risk management and control framework.

You Will Be Responsible For

Audit, Risk & Control Leadership & Execution:

Lead the planning, execution, and reporting of risk-based audit engagements across financial, operational and strategic domains, primarily in Pension Operations and Technology.
Lead project assurance engagements focused on reviewing of technology transformations and IT risk assessments, including evaluation of system development, infrastructure, cybersecurity, and application controls in multiple environments: in-house developed platforms, SaaS and “on prem” applications.
Develop engagement objectives, audit approaches, scopes, and timelines aligned with organizational strategy, risk appetite, and regulatory expectations.
Identify control gaps, assess root causes, validate remediation plans, and support residual risk acceptance where appropriate

Stakeholder Engagement & Advisory

Cultivate strong relationships with senior business partners in pensions and technology to understand processes, risks, and control environments.
Serve as a key liaison during audits and risk engagements, providing timely insights, practical recommendations, and ongoing status updates.
Translate audit and technology risk issues into clear, business-focused language for executive and senior management audiences.
Collaborate closely with Corporate Oversight functions (e.g., Compliance & Ethics, Enterprise Risk partners) to ensure consistent and effective risk management approaches.

Reporting, Insights & Follow-Up

Deliver clear, balanced, and actionable audit reports ingrained with recommendations based on root cause analysis and risk assessments for senior management and Board committees.
Partner with management to develop effective, sustainable action plans and monitor timely remediation of findings.
Develop reporting, metrics, and dashboards to highlight control effectiveness, emerging risks, and thematic issues.

Strategic Planning & Methodology

Assist IA leadership in identifying emerging risks, developing the annual audit plan, and optimizing audit methodologies, including agile, AI and data-driven audit approaches.
Contribute to the development and maintenance of the audit universe and help ensure alignment with organizational strategy and goals and regulatory requirements (where applicable).
Support the development of the annual audit plan.
Apply and promote leading practices and regulatory frameworks (e.g., COBIT, ISO, NIST, FFIEC, PCI, ITIL, agile audit methodologies).
Advance the use of data analytics, automation, artificial intelligence and technology-enabled audit techniques.

Leadership, Culture & Capability Building

Mentor, coach, and develop audit professionals, building deep technical, analytical, and stakeholder management capabilities across the IA team.
Support continuous improvement initiatives, including training, methodology enhancements, and innovation within the audit function.
Promote risk awareness and strong control discipline across the organization through formal and informal engagement.

Required Skills & Experience

University degree in accounting, finance, business, information technology, or a related field.
Professional designation preferred: CPA, CIA, and CISA, CISSP or other relevant designation considered an asset.
Significant progressive experience (typically 8+ years) in internal or external audit, technology risk or assurance.
Experience with audit and risk analytics, reporting tools, and audit management software (e.g., TeamMate, Diligent, Resolver, ACL or equivalent).
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to assess complex, interrelated processes.
Proven leadership and influencing skills, with comfort engaging senior executives and diverse stakeholder groups.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present concise, executive-ready materials.
Demonstrated ability to balance assurance, advisory, and delivery responsibilities in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
Experience with audit and risk analytics, reporting tools, and audit management software (e.g., TeamMate, Diligent, Resolver, ACL or equivalent).

Preferred Skills & Experiences

Pension Plan Administration Certificate (PPAC) is considered an asset.
Working knowledge of regulatory and control frameworks such as COBIT, ISO 27001, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ITIL, and related standards.
Ability to interpret data queries (e.g. SQL) and leverage analytics to support data driven audit and risk insights.

Build the Future of Hospitality, Entertainment & Live Experiences.

At INK Entertainment
, we don't just open restaurants or produce events—we create destinations, experiences, and brands that people remember.

From award-winning restaurants and nightlife venues to concerts, festivals, and cultural experiences, INK is redefining hospitality and entertainment across North America. You'll own the digital roadmap—from websites and CRM to paid media, SEO, marketing technology, AI, analytics, and digital customer experiences. You'll partner with leaders across Marketing, Operations, Creative, Brand Partnerships, PR, Events, and Technology to drive measurable business growth while building exceptional digital experiences.
You'll also lead and mentor our digital team, including Social Media, ensuring every digital touchpoint reflects the creativity and innovation that defines INK.

Digital Strategy

Define and execute INK's enterprise digital strategy across hospitality, entertainment, music, and live events.
Identify emerging technologies and consumer trends that create competitive advantage.
Lead digital transformation initiatives that improve customer experience and business performance.
Build the roadmap for future digital growth.

Customer Growth

Grow reservations, ticket sales, memberships, loyalty, gift card sales, and online revenue.
Develop CRM, email, SMS, and lifecycle marketing strategies that increase customer acquisition, retention, and lifetime value.
Optimize every step of the digital customer journey.

Digital Marketing

Lead paid media strategy across Google, Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Snapchat, Reddit, Spotify, and emerging platforms.
Oversee SEO, digital advertising, audience acquisition, conversion optimization, and performance marketing.
Manage agency relationships and media investments to maximize ROI.

Digital Experiences

Oversee the strategy and evolution of INK's websites, ticketing experiences, reservation platforms, and digital products.
Ensure every digital experience is intuitive, accessible, mobile-first, and conversion-focused.
Champion innovation using AI, automation, personalization, and emerging technology.

Music, Live Events & Brand Partnerships

Develop digital marketing strategies that drive awareness and ticket sales for concerts, festivals, nightlife programming, and live experiences.
Partner with artists, promoters, venues, agencies, and brand partners to amplify campaigns across digital channels.
Support sponsorship activations with measurable digital strategies that create value for partners and unforgettable experiences for guests.

Analytics & Innovation

Turn data into action through reporting, attribution, experimentation, and optimization.
Build executive dashboards and performance insights that influence business decisions.
Continuously test, learn, and improve.

Who You Are:

You're a strategic digital leader who thrives in fast-paced, creative environments. You know how to balance brand storytelling with performance marketing, and you're as comfortable discussing customer acquisition costs as you are envisioning the next big digital experience.
You bring curiosity, commercial thinking, and a passion for innovation—and you're excited to help shape what's next.

What You'll Bring:

8+ years of progressive digital marketing experience, including leadership experience.
Experience in hospitality, entertainment, live events, music, lifestyle, retail, or consumer brands.
Expertise across paid media, SEO, CRM, marketing automation, analytics, websites, and digital strategy.
Experience leading multi-brand digital ecosystems.

Set direction for cybersecurity and infrastructure risk management, ensuring gaps are identified, prioritized, and addressed.
Direct business continuity, disaster recovery, and technology resilience planning to ensure uninterrupted operations and effective risk mitigation.

Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leaders, partnering across the organization to understand needs and translate them into scalable technology solutions that enhance productivity and support business objectives.

Establish and monitor key performance indicators and service metrics to measure operational effectiveness, project outcomes, and team performance.
Oversee workforce planning, budgeting, forecasting, vendor and contract management, and financial stewardship to optimize the value of technology investments across the organization.

15+ years of progressive leadership experience in business technology, enterprise systems, business operations, or related fields, including 6+ years leading enterprise technology functions and organizational change.
Proven experience overseeing ERP platforms and enterprise business applications through implementation, stabilization, optimization, governance, adoption, and continuous improvement.
Strong ability to align technology investments with business strategy, operational effectiveness, employee experience, client value, and measurable outcomes.
Deep understanding of cybersecurity, privacy, risk management, data governance, enterprise architecture, information management, and emerging technology enablement.
Exceptional leadership, communication, relationship-building, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into practical business decisions.
Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Information Systems, Business, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline; equivalent experience will be considered.

Play a key role in advancing RJC's Purpose, Promise, Vision, and long-term strategic priorities.
Provide leadership for one of the firm's most significant business transformation initiatives through the continued evolution of our ERP platform and enterprise business systems.
Help strengthen the technology, information, and knowledge capabilities that enable our people to do their best work.
Partner with leaders across the organization to improve collaboration, decision-making, innovation, and organizational effectiveness.

Develop and execute a multi-year roadmap to transform the analytics function through AI, aligned with enterprise strategy, the AI Council, and GS1 Canada’s technology and data priorities.
Prioritize high-value use cases such as automated data preparation and reporting, insight synthesis, anomaly detection, forecasting, segmentation, churn and propensity analysis, and conversational or self-service analytics.
Redesign analyst workflows and roles to combine automation with human judgment, enabling the team to spend less time producing reports and more time interpreting results, advising leaders, and driving action.
Establish a disciplined path from experimentation to production, including use-case intake, value assessment, pilots, validation, adoption planning, controls, and scaling.
Partner with Technology and Data Governance on approved tools, architecture, secure data access, semantic models, data quality, integration, and production support; retain business ownership of analytical use cases, adoption, and outcomes.
Partner with the AI Council, Privacy, Legal, Cybersecurity, and Data Governance to ensure appropriate human oversight, transparency, confidentiality, intellectual property protection, bias testing, accuracy, and responsible use
Build team capability in AI-assisted analysis, prompt and context design, model limitations, validation, documentation, and effective human review.
Measure transformation value through adoption, time-to-insight, productivity, analytical quality, decision impact, and measurable business outcomes.

Develop talent, succession plans, and future-ready skills across business intelligence, analytics, market intelligence, and AI.

new_jobs.description:
Qui sommes-nous ?

FTI Consulting est un chef de file mondial des sociétés d’experts-conseils pour les organisations qui font face à des crises et à des transformations. Nous travaillons sur les enjeux majeurs de beaucoup de multinationales, cabinets d’avocats, banques et sociétés de financement par capitaux propres, qui sont parmi les plus importants au monde, pour créer un impact qui fait la différence. Qu’il s’agisse de résoudre des questions litigieuses, de naviguer à travers des crises, de gérer des risques et d’optimiser le rendement, nos équipes répondent rapidement aux situations complexes et dynamiques.

Chez FTI Consulting, vous travaillerez aux côtés de leaders qui ont façonné l’histoire, en aidant à régler les plus grands défis qui font les manchettes aujourd’hui. Dès le premier jour, vous ferez partie intégrante d’une équipe focalisée où vous pourrez faire une vraie différence. Vous serez entouré d’une culture ouverte et collaborative qui souscrit à la diversité, à la reconnaissance, au perfectionnement professionnel, et de façon plus importante, à vous.

Êtes-vous prêt à faire votre différence ?

Français

À propos de FTI et du poste

Le groupe Financement corporatif et restructuration de FTI Consulting accompagne les entreprises, prêteurs, investisseurs, conseils d’administration, fonds de capital-investissement et autres parties prenantes dans la gestion de défis financiers, opérationnels et stratégiques complexes. Nos professionnels travaillent aux côtés des équipes de direction afin de répondre à des enjeux de liquidité, d’améliorer la performance, d’évaluer des solutions stratégiques et d’accompagner les organisations dans des périodes de transformation, de crise ou de changement. Le groupe Financement corporatif et restructuration de FTI offre des services couvrant le redressement et la restructuration, les transactions ainsi que les initiatives de transformation d'entreprise.

FTI Consulting est un cabinet-conseil de premier plan à l’échelle mondiale comptant plus de 8 000 professionnels et des bureaux dans les principaux marchés canadiens. Notre pratique de Montréal poursuit sa croissance et offre une occasion unique de joindre une équipe entrepreneuriale tout en bénéficiant des ressources, de l’expertise et des possibilités de carrière d’un leader mondial du secteur.

Nos équipes de mission sont volontairement de taille restreinte, permettant à chacun d’assumer rapidement des responsabilités importantes, d’interagir directement avec les clients et d’accélérer son développement professionnel dès le premier jour.

À titre de directeur(trice), vous jouerez un rôle clé auprès des entreprises et des parties prenantes confrontées à des situations financières et opérationnelles complexes, en dirigeant des mandats, en développant des relations de confiance avec les clients et en contribuant à la croissance continue de notre pratique.

Exemples de mandats récents

Gestion des liquidités et préparation de flux de trésorerie prévisionnels sur 13 semaines
Revues indépendantes des opérations de l’entreprise pour des prêteurs et investisseurs
Évaluations de la performance financière et opérationnelle
Mandats de redressement et de restructuration
Procédures en vertu de la Loi sur la faillite et l’insolvabilité (LFI) et de la Loi sur les arrangements avec les créanciers des compagnies (LACC)
Transactions de fusions et acquisitions en contexte de détresse financière et évaluations d’alternatives stratégiques
Mandats de conseil auprès des parties prenantes

Ce poste convient parfaitement aux candidats souhaitant mettre à profit leur expérience en restructuration, en finance corporative, en conseil auprès des parties prenantes et en gestion tout en jouant un rôle concret dans le développement d’une pratique en forte croissance.

Ce que vous ferez

À titre de directeur(trice), vous travaillerez directement avec des équipes de direction, des prêteurs, des investisseurs, des conseillers juridiques et des professionnels chevronnés de FTI sur des mandats auprès d’entreprises canadiennes et internationales évoluant dans divers secteurs d’activité. Vous serez impliqué dans des mandats complexes, superviserez leur exécution et contribuerez au développement continu de la pratique Financement corporatif et restructuration de FTI à Montréal.

Responsabilités principales

Superviser l’exécution quotidienne de mandats de restructuration, de redressement d’entreprise et de transactions, incluant des interactions avec les équipes de direction, les conseillers juridiques, les prêteurs, les investisseurs et les autres conseillers financiers
Mettre à profit vos compétences en affaires, en comptabilité, en finance et en analyse dans le cadre de divers mandats
Examiner les états financiers et les informations opérationnelles afin d’évaluer la performance de l’entreprise et d’identifier les principaux facteurs de risque et opportunités
Préparer et réviser des projections de flux de trésorerie, des analyses de liquidité et des modèles financiers complexes
Évaluer des plans d’affaires, des initiatives de restructuration, des alternatives stratégiques et d’importants volumes de données liés aux mandats
Réaliser des revues diligentes financières et d’autres analyses en appui à des mandats de restructuration, de refinancement ou de transaction
Développer une compréhension approfondie des activités des débitrices, incluant leur performance opérationnelle et financière, leurs flux de trésorerie et leurs principaux moteurs de création de valeur
Préparer et réviser des rapports, des présentations et d’autres livrables destinés aux équipes de direction, prêteurs, investisseurs, conseils d’administration et autres parties prenantes
Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes de direction, les conseillers juridiques, les prêteurs, les investisseurs et les autres parties prenantes dans le cadre de processus de restructuration, de financement ou de transaction
Gérer les équipes de mission et offrir du mentorat, de l’encadrement et des opportunités de développement aux professionnels plus juniors
Contribuer aux initiatives de développement des affaires et à la croissance continue de la pratique de Financement corporatif et restructuration de Montréal
Ce poste nécessite des déplacements chez les clients et dans les bureaux de FTI, selon les besoins

Votre développement chez FTI

Chez FTI Consulting, nous investissons activement dans le développement professionnel et la réussite à long terme de nos employés.

Ce que nous vous offrons

L’opportunité de participer à des mandats de restructuration et de financement d’envergure
Une exposition directe auprès de dirigeants, de membres de conseils d’administration, de prêteurs et d’investisseurs
Une plateforme favorisant votre progression au sein de l’un des principaux cabinets-conseils en restructuration et en financement corporatif au monde
Des occasions de développer des relations clients durables et d’approfondir vos compétences en développement des affaires
Une collaboration avec des professionnels de premier plan en restructuration et en financement corporatif au Canada et à l’international
Des programmes de formation formels et informels axés sur le développement technique, professionnel et du leadership
Une expérience concrète dans une variété d’industries, de situations d’affaires et de types de transactions
La possibilité de jouer un rôle important dans la croissance continue de la pratique montréalaise de FTI
Un coach de carrière dédié pour soutenir votre progression et votre développement professionnel

Une expérience préalable en restructuration, en redressement d’entreprise ou en insolvabilité, est requise. Nous recherchons des candidats possédant de solides aptitudes en comptabilité, en analyse financière et en résolution de problèmes et souhaitant bâtir une carrière à long terme en restructuration et en financement corporatif.

Ce qu’il vous faut pour réussir

Qualifications de base

Titre professionnel CPA requis.
7+ années d’expérience pertinente au sein d’un cabinet de services professionnels, notamment en comptabilité publique, consultation, financement corporatif, services transactionnels ou dans un environnement similaire.
Solide compréhension des états financiers, des fonctions corporatives et du fonctionnement des entreprises, incluant une expérience dans l’analyse des flux de trésorerie, des prévisions de liquidités, des projections financières et des plans d’affaires.
Maîtrise avancée de la modélisation financière sous Excel ainsi que solides capacités d’analyse et de résolution de problèmes.
Excellente maîtrise du français et de l’anglais, tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit.
Disponibilité pour se déplacer chez les clients et dans les bureaux de FTI.

Les candidats doivent être légalement autorisés à travailler au Canada à temps plein (aucun parrainage pour un permis de travail ou un visa n’est offert pour ce poste).

Qualifications privilégiées

Les titres MBA, CFA, CIRP et/ou CBV constituent des atouts importants.
Expérience préalable en restructuration, en redressement d’entreprise, en financement corporatif et/ou en services transactionnels.
Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale, incluant la rédaction de rapports et la préparation de présentations.
Expérience dans la gestion de priorités multiples et la réalisation d’un travail de grande qualité dans un environnement de services professionnels dynamique et exigeant.
Fort intérêt pour la finance, le conseil et l’accompagnement des clients dans des situations d’affaires complexes.
Capacité et volonté d’apprendre, de s’adapter et de réussir dans un environnement en constante évolution afin de répondre aux besoins des clients.

Pourquoi FTI Consulting?

Travailler directement avec des professionnels chevronnés et des clients dès votre arrivée
Être exposé à certaines des situations les plus complexes et les plus en vue du marché
Développer une combinaison unique d’expérience en comptabilité, finance, conseil et restructuration
Joindre une pratique montréalaise en forte croissance offrant d’excellentes possibilités d’avancement
Développer un réseau auprès de dirigeants d’entreprise, prêteurs, investisseurs et conseillers juridiques
Bénéficier du mentorat de professionnels reconnus dans les domaines de la restructuration et de la finance corporative
Faire partie d’une culture entrepreneuriale, collaborative et stimulante soutenue par les ressources d’un cabinet mondial
Construire votre carrière au sein d’un cabinet reconnu mondialement comme un chef de file en financement corporatif, restructuration et services-conseils en redressement

Si vous recherchez une occasion stimulante et enrichissante combinant analyse financière, interaction avec les clients et résolution de problèmes dans des situations à fort impact, nous vous invitons à soumettre votre candidature.
